rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / THE STANDARD LIBRARY / CHAPTER 35

slides.title: Date and time
slides.main: Store and calculate in UTC; convert to local time only to display.

items.title: Format
items.sub: To string and back; ISO for storage

slides.title: date, time, datetime
slides.sub: Immutable objects that can be compared and sorted
slides.main: weekday() counts from zero, where zero is Monday; replace returns a copy.

body.text:
from datetime import date, time, datetime

d = date(2024, 2, 29)
t = time(14, 30)
dt = datetime(2024, 2, 29, 14, 30)
print(d, t, dt)
print(d.year, d.month, d.day, d.weekday())
print(dt.replace(hour=9))
print(date(2024, 3, 1) > d)

slides.title: timedelta
slides.main: timedelta has no months or years: their length varies, so “plus a month” is done by hand.

body.text:
from datetime import date, timedelta

d = date(2024, 2, 28)
print(d + timedelta(days=2))
print(date(2025, 1, 1) - date(2024, 12, 25))
delta = timedelta(hours=1, minutes=30)
print(delta.total_seconds(), delta * 2)

slides.title: Formatting
slides.main: ISO notation sorts as text in time order: the best storage format.

body.text:
from datetime import datetime

dt = datetime(2024, 3, 5, 9, 7, 3)
print(dt.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"))
print(dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
print(dt.isoformat())
%Y year, %m month, %d day, %H hours, %M minutes, %S seconds.

slides.title: Parsing a string
slides.main: Python will not create a nonexistent date: parsing is already a check.

body.text:
from datetime import datetime

d = datetime.strptime("05.03.2024", "%d.%m.%Y")
print(d, d.year)
print(datetime.fromisoformat("2024-03-05T09:07:03"))
try:
    datetime.strptime("30.02.2024", "%d.%m.%Y")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)

slides.title: Time zones
slides.main: Naive and aware can't be compared: store UTC, convert via astimezone.

body.text:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

utc = datetime(2024, 6, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
msk = utc.astimezone(ZoneInfo("Europe/Moscow"))
print(utc, msk)
print(msk.utcoffset())
naive = datetime(2024, 6, 1, 12, 0)
try:
    naive < utc
except TypeError as e:
    print(e)

2024-06-01 12:00:00+00:00 2024-06-01 15:00:00+03:00
3:00:00
can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes

slides.title: The time module
slides.main: For timing use perf_counter: it ignores system clock changes.

body.text:
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

start = time.perf_counter()
time.sleep(0.01)
print(time.perf_counter() - start >= 0.01)
print(datetime(1970, 1, 2, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp())
print(datetime.fromtimestamp(86400, tz=timezone.utc))
Unix time: seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC.

slides.title: Ranges and comparison
slides.main: All familiar arithmetic, comparison, and generators; only the types are new.

body.text:
from datetime import date, timedelta

start, end = date(2024, 3, 1), date(2024, 3, 10)
days = [start + timedelta(days=i) for i in range((end - start).days + 1)]
workdays = [d for d in days if d.weekday() < 5]
print(len(days), len(workdays))
print(min(days), max(days).isocalendar()[1])

slides.title: calendar and age
slides.main: Age is not “days / 365”: subtract years, adjust if the birthday hasn't come yet.

body.text:
import calendar
from datetime import date

weekday, days = calendar.monthrange(2024, 2)
print(calendar.isleap(2024), int(weekday), days)
print(date(2024, 2, days))

def age(born, today):
    years = today.year - born.year
    if (today.month, today.day) < (born.month, born.day):
        years -= 1
    return years

print(age(date(2000, 6, 15), date(2024, 6, 14)), age(date(2000, 6, 15), date(2024, 6, 15)))

slides.title: Typical tasks
slides.sub: To New Year, weekday, log by dates
slides.main: A date at the start of a log line, and grouping by day takes one line.

body.text:
from collections import Counter
from datetime import date

today = date(2024, 12, 20)
new_year = date(2025, 1, 1)
print((new_year - today).days)
names = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
print(names[date(2000, 1, 1).weekday()])
log = ["2024-03-01 error", "2024-03-01 ok", "2024-03-02 ok"]
print(Counter(line.split()[0] for line in log))

slides.title: Dates and JSON
slides.sub: Write as a string, read it back
slides.main: The storage format is part of the contract: define “to string” and “from string” in one place.

body.text:
import json
from datetime import datetime

event = {"name": "deadline", "at": datetime(2024, 5, 1, 10, 0)}
text = json.dumps(event, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)
print(text)
back = json.loads(text)
print(datetime.fromisoformat(back["at"]).month)

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: A month is not thirty days; date strings are not dates
slides.main: Compare date objects, not strings in a nonstandard format.

body.text:
from datetime import date, timedelta

d = date(2024, 1, 31)
print(d + timedelta(days=30))
try:
    d.replace(month=2)
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
print((date(2024, 3, 1) - date(2023, 3, 1)).days)
print(date(2024, 5, 3) < date(2024, 5, 10), "3.5.2024" < "10.5.2024")

2024-03-01
day 31 must be in range 1..29 for month 2 in year 2024
366
True False
